judge_signature_consistency.notes: ADR-SAG-0009 r-7 amendment (docs/architecture.md:286-289) says judge takes the per-send &SendTrace (ADR-SAG-0031). REQ-SAG-0103 r-7 row (docs/requirements.md:210) says the contract is unchanged except that judge takes the per-send &SendTrace and model_id() is added. sprint-r-7 D-section (lines 603-604, 763) gives the signature judge(&self, req: &JudgeRequest, trace: &SendTrace) and labels it a REQ-SAG-0103 amendment. plan.md:559 lists the same hand-off. The ADR-SAG-0031 text at architecture.md:1636 says the engine passes the SendTrace to judge. Both records use &SendTrace by reference, and SendTrace is not carried on the JudgeRequest, which matches RBP-F001. The pre-existing rows (docs/requirements.md:39 and :199) still describe the a-1 and r-1 contract without the trace argument. They are historical rows that the r-7 row amends, not a contradiction. The Phase A docs (docs/plans/phase-a/plan.md:92 and sprint-a-4-backend-jev.md:63) keep the old two-argument signature. They are historical Phase A plans superseded by A.1, so I raise no finding. One minor observation, not a finding: the plan.md:717 index row for ADR-SAG-0009 does not mention the judge signature, but it is a summary row and the ADR text itself is complete.
